title: Runner bean and split pea dal

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or plain cupboard staple: split peas, fresh vegetables, oil, spices, lemon and coriander.

supermarket.reason: Yellow split peas, runner beans, fresh chilli, coriander and the spices are all everyday Tesco items at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only one lidded pan, a knife and a board, and the technique is simple simmering.

works.reason: 250g split peas in 1.2 litres of water with 400g runner beans makes a sensible dal for four, and 55 minutes of simmering should soften the peas, though older peas may need a little longer.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes is fair for slicing the onions and runner beans and chopping the tomatoes, and the steps add up to roughly the 60 minutes of cooking printed.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: 400g of runner beans is a large share of the dish, so they are central rather than a garnish, and a dal suits a July lunch.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are brief, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: A filling pulse-and-vegetable dal is real, sustaining food that a family would happily cook again.
